result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers ground the look in roadside phone use and give concrete colours, type, shape and layout rules, and both cover the instructor and learner/parent sides with one shared look. B goes further on things instructors actually hit: poor signal, failed payments, no-shows and an edit-ready skill vocabulary. It also flags its currency and terms as guesses to swap out. A states invented facts as given (a £40 lesson price and a 90-second window between lessons) and leans a little harder on car costume (number plates). Neither answer gives system font fallbacks. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both briefs are concrete and grounded in the roadside phone use, with ledger-style rows instead of cards, a light theme for glare and one yellow accent. B gives more detail in places, including a secondary grey, an elevation rule, a voice section and a navigation limit, but it invents facts: an '~90 seconds' gap between lessons, '£40' and the learner name 'Sam'. A avoids invented facts, uses '£__' and says which choices are guesses, and covers more of the learner/parent flow and the edge cases (offline sync, failed payment, no-show).
